title: SAP and ERP: is the system that moves your money patched, closed and watched?
short: Apply SAP and Oracle security patches every month, exploited ones within 72 hours, and keep SAP support packages under 24 months old.
answer: This month, take every ERP web component that doesn't need to be public off the internet, and apply each month's SAP Security Notes and Oracle patches within the patching sheet's deadlines. Then close the paths inside (RFC gateway, trusted connections, standard users, SAP_ALL in production) and keep the Security Audit Log on and in your SIEM, so someone reviews every emergency and admin session.
audience: SAP Basis, security and IT teams running SAP ECC, S/4HANA, RISE or BTP, and teams running Oracle or Microsoft ERP systems

blocks.title: If you only do five things

items.title: Take ERP web components off the internet.
items.text: Publish only the HTTP paths partners need, through a reverse proxy in front of SAP Web Dispatcher[^app42], and never the gateway, message server or start service ports[^ports]. Extortion groups stole data through Oracle E-Business Suite and PeopleSoft zero-days in 2025 and 2026[^gtigebs][^gtigps].

items.title: Patch every month, by exploitation and exposure.
items.text: SAP releases Security Notes on the second Tuesday of each month[^sapnotes], and Oracle now patches monthly[^oraalerts]. A ransomware group weaponized an SAP NetWeaver flaw a day after disclosure[^mddr].

items.title: Keep support packages under 24 months old.
items.text: SAP fixes new high and critical notes only for support packages shipped in the last 24 months[^sapnotes].

items.title: Lock down the RFC gateway.
items.text: Use SAP's restrictive secinfo and reginfo files[^gwsec], delete unused RFC connections and store no passwords in connections from development to production[^app42].

items.title: Take SAP_ALL out of production.
items.text: BSI allows SAP_ALL, SAP_NEW and S_DEVELOP change rights in production only for emergency users, whose actions are logged[^app42]. Turn on the Security Audit Log in all clients[^sentprep].

items.title: Which notes apply to which system?
items.text: System Recommendations in SAP Solution Manager matches new Security Notes and HotNews against each system[^sysrec]; otherwise filter All Security Notes in SAP for Me[^sapnotes].

items.title: How fast must each one go in?
items.text: Use the patching sheet's tiers: exploited (in KEV[^kev]) first, then Critical and High notes within 14 days on internet-facing systems and 30 days inside[^sapoct26].

items.title: Did the fix reach production?
items.text: Implement ABAP corrections in development, transport them on[^rr] and record each note's status per system[^app42].

items.title: Is the server still talking to the internet?
items.text: Block outbound traffic from ERP servers, as Google advises for EBS[^gtigebs]; it can stop an attack after a break-in.

blocks.title: Close the paths inside
items: **Block function modules nobody calls.** In UCON's final phase, remote-enabled function modules not assigned to a communication assembly can't be called from outside[^ucon].
**Treat trusted RFC like a stored password.** Never let development or test systems trust into production[^app42].
**Lock the standard users.** Lock SAP*, DDIC and EARLYWATCH but keep SAP* in every client, and check with report RSUSR003[^stdusers].
**Run jobs as technical users.** Background jobs run as System users, and no standard user runs jobs or RFC connections[^app42].

blocks.title: Powerful rights and emergency access
items: **Remove debug and replace.** S_DEVELOP with object type DEBUG and change rights lets users alter accounting data in memory without a trace[^dsag].
**Remove all-table access.** No production user should display every table through SE16 with S_TABU_DIS for all groups[^dsag].

**Review every firefighter session.** Unlock emergency users per ticket and log everything[^app42]. SAP Access Control's Emergency Access Management sends each session's log to a reviewer, if the system records it[^eam].
**Protect vendor bank details.** Mark bank fields as sensitive, so a second user must confirm changes before the automatic payment run; manual payments aren't blocked[^dualctl].

blocks.title: Logs, transports and custom code
items: **Get the audit log to your SIEM.** Log all message types; Microsoft calls the cost difference minimal[^sentprep]. Microsoft Sentinel's SAP solution charges hourly per production system and needs SAP Integration Suite[^sentinel][^sentprep].
**Make production unchangeable.** Build roles and code only in development and move them by transport[^app42].
**Check code at transport release** with the ABAP Test Cockpit[^atc]. Its security checks, Code Vulnerability Analyzer, need a separate license on premises, or SAP BTP ABAP Environment[^cva].
**Follow APP.4.6 in custom ABAP.** Check AUTHORITY-CHECK results; avoid dynamic Open SQL, ADBC and INSERT REPORT[^app46].

blocks.title: When ERP security fixes stop
items: **End of 2027.** Mainstream maintenance ends for SAP ERP 6.0, EHP 6 to 8[^bs7], and SAP Solution Manager[^sysrec].
**2028 to 2030.** Optional extended maintenance costs 2 percentage points more[^bs7]. Then, in customer-specific maintenance, SAP considers new high and critical notes for 12 months only[^sapnotes].
**RISE transition option.** Security patches from 2031 to 2033 for systems moved to SAP ERP, private edition on HANA by the end of 2030[^transopt].
**Dynamics GP.** Support ends on 31 December 2029, security patches on 30 April 2031[^gp].

blocks.title: What to demand from RISE and partners
items: **Know what RISE leaves to you.** Finding relevant notes and implementing application notes need Cloud Application Services packages; testing and the application security concept stay yours[^rr].
**Own the SIEM rules.** SAP's LogServ is optional, and SAP doesn't confirm receipt, write correlation rules or watch alerts[^rr].
**Write it into the contract.** Monthly patch status per system, fixed times for exploited and Critical notes, personal partner accounts. See the third-party-risk sheet.

blocks.title: What changed in 2026
items: **Oracle patches monthly.** Critical Security Patch Updates, first on 28 May, fill the months between quarterly Critical Patch Updates[^oraalerts].
**PeopleSoft zero-day.** ShinyHunters exploited CVE-2026-35273 from 27 May, before Oracle's 10 June alert[^gtigps].
**Oracle Payments exploited.** KEV listed CVE-2026-46817, an unauthenticated takeover of Oracle Payments, on 15 July[^kev].
**ECC on RISE until 2035.** Since 13 October, transition option subscriptions may run to the end of 2035[^transopt].

blocks.title: What you can skip
items: **Buying threat detection first.** Sentinel for SAP or SAP Enterprise Threat Detection sees little while the audit log is off and notes are months behind.
**Applying every note on Patch Day.** Support Package Security Notes can wait for the next support package[^sapnotes].
**A complete SoD rule set before cleanup.** Removing SAP_ALL, debug and replace and all-table access cuts more risk than months of tuning rules.

blocks.title: Mistakes that cost the most
items: **Leaving unused components installed.** Visual Composer was exploited in 2025, with known ransomware use[^kev], and got another 9.9 note in October 2026[^sapoct26].
**Falling behind on cumulative patches.** Oracle's fix for CVE-2025-61882 needed the October 2023 Critical Patch Update first[^oraebsalert].
**Assuming RISE applies every note.** Without the packages, you find and request them yourself[^rr].

blocks.title: What this looks like at your size

columns.title: Small team, no security staff
items: Ask your ERP partner for a monthly list of applied notes and proof that no ERP login is public.
In Business Central, limit SUPER, which reaches everything the license allows[^bcperm], and get an email when an IBAN changes[^bcaudit].

columns.title: Growing, with IT or security staff
items: Run Patch Day with System Recommendations and track each note into production.
Move to restrictive gateway files, start UCON logging and alert on emergency user logons.

columns.title: Enterprise or regulated
items: Use SAP Access Control for firefighter IDs and BSI APP.4.2 or the DSAG guide as audit baseline[^app42][^dsag].
Decide by mid-2027 between extended maintenance, the transition option and finishing S/4HANA.
